description: DalíPE is a one-person team from Puno, Peru, with an academic background in Systems Engineering and Artificial Intelligence at the Private University of Trujillo (UPRIT). Its member has skills in programming, web development, data analysis, and scientific research. The team focuses on applying technology and artificial intelligence to develop innovative solutions that address real-world challenges.
summary: TITICACA CONTRAST is an interactive climate analysis platform focused on four watersheds in Puno, Peru: Ramis, Coata, Ilave, and Huancané. Using NASA GPM-IMERG V07 satellite precipitation data and official watershed boundaries, the platform analyzes historical rainfall trends, compares changes between watersheds, and evaluates statistical significance. It provides interactive maps, time-series charts, and evidence-based findings to support environmental research, education, and water-resource planning.
details:
TITICACA CONTRAST: One Lake, Different Climate Realities

TITICACA CONTRAST is an interactive web application developed to investigate historical precipitation patterns in four watersheds of Lake Titicaca in Puno, Peru: Ramis, Coata, Ilave, and Huancané.

The platform addresses the NASA Space Apps challenge "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" by identifying how precipitation has changed over time and evaluating whether neighboring watersheds exhibit statistically distinguishable trends.

How it works

The application processes NASA GPM-IMERG Final V07 monthly precipitation data and combines them with official watershed boundaries from Peru's National Water Authority (ANA). Satellite precipitation estimates are spatially aggregated for each watershed and converted into monthly and annual rainfall totals.

Users can explore an interactive geographic map, select individual watersheds, examine historical precipitation charts, compare two watersheds, and review statistical findings.

The analysis covers 24 complete years, from 2001 to 2024. Theil-Sen estimation measures precipitation trends, Mann-Kendall evaluates their statistical significance, and pairwise comparisons use Newey-West HAC standard errors with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction.

Main findings

All four watersheds exhibit statistically significant decreasing trends in annual precipitation. However, none of the six pairwise comparisons establishes a statistically significant difference in trend after multiple-testing correction. These results highlight the importance of distinguishing observed climate changes from statistically confirmed differences between regions.

Technology and innovation

The project combines Python-based scientific processing with a React and TypeScript web interface, interactive Leaflet maps, OpenStreetMap cartography, data visualizations, and an interactive geographic presentation. The application is hosted on GitHub Pages, with its source code and research outputs available for inspection.

Its distinctive contribution is a watershed-level comparison of precipitation trends rather than a single regional average, making satellite climate evidence easier to explore and interpret.

Intended impact

TITICACA CONTRAST supports environmental research, climate education, and evidence-informed water resource planning in the Lake Titicaca region. It provides historical analysis, not real-time weather forecasts or proof of climate-change causation.
